firstMismatch.message: Replay error: gb is not defined

mismatch.message: Replay error: gb is not defined

summary: A monster wand-of-striking ray that hits a shop door exposed two defects in muse.c:mbhit’s JavaScript path. The door-break branch referenced an undefined gb instead of state.gb, stopping replay. After repairing that state reference, C/JS diagnostics showed cloned monster-turn planning advanced the live RNG: the planner’s makeknown/discover_object call dropped rawEnv, so exercise_nonphysical fell back to module-global rn2. Passing rawEnv preserves the planner clone and leaves the caller RNG aligned with C.

source.branch: When a monster wand ray reaches a shop door and doorlock breaks it, C marks the wand known when visible and adds zero-cost shop damage at gb.bhitpos. In the JS planner clone, the same discovery call must use its cloned random environment.

evidence: C source muse.c:1734-1814 defines mbhit. Its WAN_STRIKING door branch calls doorlock, then makeknown(otyp) when gz.zap_oseen, and add_damage(gb.bhitpos.x, gb.bhitpos.y, 0L) when a shop door is broken. The JS branch uses state.gb for bhitpos and passes rawEnv to discover_object.

C macro hack.h:1530 maps makeknown(x) to discover_object((x), TRUE, TRUE, TRUE); JS o_init.js:discover_object accepts the caller environment. Omitting rawEnv during cloned monster-turn planning lets its nested exercise draw use module-global RNG.

Instrumented C trace and JS loader trace are retained under .cache/task-validation/v71-shop-ray/. They identify the planner call path use_offensive -> mbhit -> discover_object -> exercise_nonphysical -> exerciseAttribute and the live-stream shift at C rng call 3195 / JS step 506. The temporary instrumentation did not modify the recipe or recording.

After the fix, JS-only replay against the immutable C recording matched all 559 screens, 559 cursors, and 3216 RNG calls (run-XLvOSw, receipt under /tmp/teleport-validation-1000/run-XLvOSw/receipt.json).
